Pipeline stage: item generation

Source: R/pipeline-items.R
generate_items.Rd

generate_items() writes candidate items for the blueprint's cells with a large language model through the ellmer package, using the provider set up with mv_ask_setup() (Claude, OpenAI or a local Ollama model). Multiple-choice items come with a key and a rationale for every option; open-ended items come with a scoring rubric that has a descriptor and an anchor response for every score point. add_items() adds items written by people (or another generator) to the same pool, so the checks treat both alike.

Usage

generate_items(
  p,
  n = NULL,
  cells = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  n_options = 4,
  instructions = NULL,
  provider = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  verify = TRUE,
  batch = 5
)

add_items(p, items)

verify_items(p, ids = NULL, provider = NULL, model = NULL, .rerun = TRUE)

Arguments

p

a pipeline; generate_items() needs a blueprint from set_blueprint().

n

number of items to write per cell and item type. Defaults to coverage_ratio times the cell's target count, less the items the cell already has.

cells

optional cells to write for (by name, as in p$blueprint$cells$cell); defaults to all.

type

item types to write; defaults to the blueprint's.

n_options

number of options of a multiple-choice item.

instructions

optional extra instructions for the item writer, such as a style guide or a reading passage.

provider, model

the language model; see mv_ask_setup().

verify

logical; run the verifying pass on multiple-choice items.

batch

number of items to ask for in one call.

items

for add_items(), a data frame with one row per item and columns stem, cell, type ("mc" or "open", default "mc"), the options either as a list column options or as columns A, B, C, ..., key (the letter of the correct option), and optionally id, rubric (a list column of data frames with columns score, descriptor and anchor) and source (default "human").

ids

items to verify; defaults to every multiple-choice item not yet verified.

.rerun

internal.

Value

The pipeline with the new items in p$items: a tibble with one row per item (id, cell, type, stem, options, key, rationales, rubric, max_score, grade, source, status and the verification results).

Details

With verify = TRUE (the default), a second, independent model call answers each multiple-choice item without seeing the key and judges each distractor (verify_items() runs this pass on its own).

The checks (thresholds from mv_rules()):

  • invalid_key (block): a multiple-choice key that is not one of the options.

  • key_check (block): the verifying pass chose another answer, or found more than one defensible answer.

  • rubric_incomplete (block): an open-ended item without a descriptor and an anchor response for every score point from 0 to the maximum.

  • distractor (review): a distractor the verifying pass judged implausible or partly correct.

  • near_duplicate (review): two items whose wording overlaps by more than duplicate_sim (Jaccard similarity of their words).

  • coverage (review): a blueprint cell with fewer than coverage_ratio times its target count of items (items are lost in review and field testing).

  • readability (info): item text above the blueprint's grade level (Flesch-Kincaid grade).

Generated items are drafts: they need human content and sensitivity review before they are field-tested, and every item records its source.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
p <- set_blueprint(mv_pipeline(), c(Fractions = 4, Decimals = 4),
                   construct = "Grade 5 number sense", use = "diagnostic",
                   population = "Grade 5 students", grade_level = 5)
p <- generate_items(p, n = 3)
p$items
flags(p)
} # }
